subject: Mathematics
source: Paraphrased exemplars in the style of Edexcel GCSE (9-1) Mathematics 1MA1 Papers 1, 2 and 3 (2017 onwards). Stems are author-original; mark allocations and command verbs match published mark schemes.

exemplars.markScheme: M1 for correct power of 10 (-4). A1 for 4.82 × 10^{-4}.
exemplars.source: Edexcel 1MA1 Paper 1F style — standard form conversion

exemplars.markScheme: M1 for expanding bracket to 4x − 12. M1 for correct rearranging. A1 for x = 8.5 or 17/2.
exemplars.source: Edexcel 1MA1 Paper 1F style — linear equation with brackets

exemplars.stem: Solve x² − 7x + 12 = 0 by factorising. Show all steps.
exemplars.markScheme: M1 for finding two numbers that multiply to give 12 and add to −7. M1 for (x − 3)(x − 4) = 0. A1 for x = 3 and x = 4.

exemplars.stem: Solve the simultaneous equations 3x + 2y = 16 and x − y = 2 algebraically.
exemplars.markScheme: M1 for valid method (substitution or elimination). M1 for solving for one variable. A1 for x = 4. A1 for y = 2.
exemplars.source: Edexcel 1MA1 Paper 2H style — linear simultaneous equations

exemplars.stem: y is directly proportional to x. When x = 6, y = 21. Find the value of y when x = 14.
exemplars.markScheme: M1 for setting up y = kx. M1 for k = 3.5. A1 for y = 49.
exemplars.source: Edexcel 1MA1 Paper 2F style — direct proportion with constant

exemplars.stem: An investment of £4500 earns 2.4% compound interest per year. Calculate the value of the investment after 3 years. Give your answer to the nearest penny.
exemplars.markScheme: M1 for use of multiplier 1.024. M1 for 4500 × 1.024³. A1 for £4831.74.

exemplars.stem: ABCD is a square. AB = 12 cm. The midpoint of CD is M. Calculate the length of AM, leaving your answer in surd form.
exemplars.markScheme: M1 for identifying right-angled triangle. M1 for AM² = 12² + 6². M1 for AM² = 180. M1 for √180 = 6√5. A1 for AM = 6√5 cm.
exemplars.source: Edexcel 1MA1 Paper 1H style — Pythagoras with surd answer

exemplars.stem: A cone has volume 480 cm³. A larger cone, similar to the first, has linear dimensions twice as large. Calculate the volume of the larger cone.
exemplars.markScheme: M1 for recognising volume scale factor = (linear scale factor)³. M1 for 2³ = 8. M1 for 480 × 8. A1 for 3840 cm³.
exemplars.source: Edexcel 1MA1 Paper 3H style — similarity with volume scale factor

exemplars.stem: There are 30 students in a class. 18 study French and 14 study Spanish. 6 study both languages. A student is chosen at random. Calculate the probability that the student studies neither French nor Spanish.
exemplars.markScheme: M1 for Venn diagram or set reasoning. M1 for 18 + 14 − 6 = 26 studying at least one. M1 for 30 − 26 = 4. A1 for 4/30 = 2/15.
exemplars.source: Edexcel 1MA1 Paper 3H style — Venn diagram probability
